rationale.conceptual: The method uses the established Lieb-Wu Bethe Ansatz equations with specific boundary conditions and quantum numbers for the antiferromagnetic state. Implementation requires translating the mathematical structure into a working numerical solver and correctly handling the root-finding, which is non-trivial but well-documented in the paper.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has three sequential stages: solving the equations for multiple L and g values, fitting expansion coefficients, and verifying exact terms. All stages use standard libraries (numpy/scipy) and produce simple CSV/JSON artifacts with no external data dependencies or complex orchestration.

The numerical implementation of these nonlinear equations, setting up correct quantum numbers, and iterative root-finding requires understanding of integrable systems but uses standard methods.
